title: ML-DSA (FIPS 204) signature engine: KeyGen, Sign (deterministic or hedged, with external mu) and Verify for ML-DSA-44, -65 and -87, with a SHAKE128 / SHAKE256 Keccak core, NTT polynomial unit and a 32 KiB key / signature / message buffer

fields.desc: operation: 0 KeyGen, 1 Sign, 2 Verify (3 is reserved: START sets ERR)
parameter set: 0 ML-DSA-44, 1 ML-DSA-65, 2 ML-DSA-87 (3 is reserved: START sets ERR)
buffer read: while set and the engine is idle, the word at the pointer is fetched into DATA_OUT and the pointer advances
Sign and Verify take mu (64 bytes at 0x2FC0) from the buffer instead of computing H(tr || M')
bytes of M' at 0x4000 (Sign and Verify without ext_mu); above 16384 START sets ERR
word address (byte address / 4) in the 32 KiB buffer
run CTRL.op on CTRL.pset; ignored while busy
load the buffer pointer from PTR

regs.name: DATA_IN
regs.desc: Buffer write: the word goes to the pointer (little-endian bytes) and the pointer advances; taken while the engine is idle

regs.name: DATA_OUT
regs.desc: Buffer read: the word fetched while CTRL.hr_en is set; reading it fetches the next

regs.name: STATUS
regs.desc: Engine state and the last operation's result

fields.desc: an operation is running (the buffer port is closed)
Verify: the signature was rejected (held from DONE to the next START)
Sign: attempts of the rejection loop (held from DONE to the next START)

irqs.name: DONE
irqs.desc: the operation finished: results are in the buffer, STATUS.fail / tries are valid

irqs.name: ERR
irqs.desc: START with a reserved op or parameter set, or MLEN above 16384 without ext_mu: nothing was run

features: FIPS 204 ML-DSA.KeyGen_internal, Sign_internal and Verify_internal (Algorithms 6, 7, 8) for all three parameter sets; bit-exact against the NIST ACVP vectors. Sign is deterministic (rnd = 0) or hedged (rnd from the host); Sign and Verify take M' from the buffer or an external mu.
Verify checks everything FIPS 204 does: ||z|| < gamma1 - beta, the hint encoding (HintBitUnpack's ordering, row-end and zero-padding rules) and c~ = c~'. STATUS.fail holds the result.
Keccak-f[1600] at one round per clock for SHAKE128 and SHAKE256; one byte absorbed per clock, up to three bytes per clock squeezed into the samplers.

Polynomial unit: one NTT / inverse NTT butterfly, pointwise product, sample or packed coefficient per clock on 43 polynomial slots, through a 6-stage pipeline; mod q = 2^23 - 2^13 + 1 by three folds of 2^23 = 2^13 - 1 (adders only). The matrix A is sampled on the fly (RejNTTPoly) straight into a multiply-accumulate and never stored.

Clock counts: KeyGen about 26k / 41k / 61k, Verify about 32k / 47k / 70k, Sign about 63k / 91k / 128k per attempt of the rejection loop for ML-DSA-44 / 65 / 87 (FIPS 204 expects 4.25 / 5.1 / 3.85 attempts on average), plus about one clock per byte of M'.
notes: Buffer map (byte addresses; word address = byte address / 4): 0x0000 pk (32 + 320 k bytes; KeyGen output, Verify input), 0x0A20 sk (KeyGen output, Sign input), 0x1D40 sig (Sign output, Verify input), 0x2F60 xi (KeyGen input, 32), 0x2FA0 rnd (Sign input, 32; zero for the deterministic variant), 0x2FC0 mu (input with CTRL.ext_mu, 64), 0x4000 M' (MLEN bytes, at most 16384). 0x2F80 and 0x3000-0x3FFF are the engine's scratch.
The host formats M' (FIPS 204 Algorithms 2-5: 0 || |ctx| || ctx || M for ML-DSA, 1 || |ctx| || ctx || OID || PH(M) for HashML-DSA) and supplies xi and rnd: the core has no random-number source.
Sign's run time depends on the number of attempts of the rejection loop (STATUS.tries), as in FIPS 204; the attempts themselves run the same sequence of steps whatever the secret values.

DATA_OUT prefetches: with CTRL.hr_en set, the word at the pointer is fetched as soon as DATA_OUT is empty, so after the last word wanted one more has been fetched. Clear hr_en and read DATA_OUT once more (or check FLAGS) before loading a new pointer.
Not implemented: masking or other power / EM side-channel protection; fault-attack countermeasures; a bound on the number of Sign attempts.
sequence: Write the inputs: PTR = word address, CMD.hp_load = 1, then the words to DATA_IN (KeyGen: xi; Sign: sk, rnd and M' or mu; Verify: pk, sig and M' or mu). Write MLEN.
CTRL = op | pset << 2 | ext_mu << 5, CMD.start = 1; wait for IRQ_STATUS.DONE (or STATUS.busy = 0). Verify: STATUS.fail = 0 accepts the signature.
Read the outputs: PTR = word address, CMD.hp_load = 1, CTRL.hr_en = 1, then read DATA_OUT once per word; clear CTRL.hr_en and read DATA_OUT once more to drop the prefetched word.
verification: Test vectors (tb/ML_DSA_vec.hex, `make -f Makefile.ML_DSA vec ACVP=...` rebuilds them): random cases from the FIPS 204 model scripts/mldsa/mldsa_ref.py (per parameter set a KeyGen, a deterministic and a hedged Sign, external mu, Verify of valid signatures and of ones with a modified c~, z, hint encoding or message; for ML-DSA-44 Sign cases picked for the rare rejections: too many hints, exactly omega hints, ||c t0|| >= gamma2, an empty and the longest M') and NIST ACVP cases (one per internal-interface group of the keyGen, sigGen and sigVer files). The model itself passes all 615 vectors of those NIST ACVP files.

The core checker computes every step the engine takes on its own: the Keccak sponge (its own Keccak-f[1600] from the FIPS 202 rotation and round-constant rules) for every byte absorbed and squeezed, and NTT, inverse NTT, pointwise products, RejNTTPoly, RejBoundedPoly, ExpandMask, SampleInBall, BitPack / SimpleBitPack, Power2Round, Decompose, MakeHint, UseHint and HintBitPack / HintBitUnpack (with every reject condition) from a copy of their inputs, as FIPS 204 writes them; plus the Sign loop, the Verify result, the host port and control rules.

Exhaustive checks (python3 scripts/formal/exhaust_ml_dsa.py): the three reduction folds for every high part, the last for every input, Decompose, UseHint and Power2Round for every r < q (both gamma2), addq / subq for every a, CoeffFromHalfByte, the zeta table and the Keccak round constants against their definitions.
